name: Hemendra Kothari
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Veteran investment banker Hemendra Kothari founded Mumbai-based DSP Mutual Fund in 2008.
He founded the firm in partnership with BlackRock but bought out BlackRock's stake ten years later.
Kothari started his career with family firm D.S. Purbhoodas & Co before founding financial services firm DSP Financial Consultants in 1975.
He partnered with Merrill Lynch in 1995 but sold his 57% stake in tranches between 2005 and 2009.
His daughter Aditi Kothari Desai is chairperson at DSP.
forbes_facts: A wildlife enthusiast, he founded the Wildlife Conservation Trust and has named meeting rooms at his office after tiger reserves.
His great-grandfather was one of the founders of the Bombay Stock Exchange.
His younger brother Yogesh Kothari, founded and runs specialty chemicals company Alkyl Amines.

name: Charlwin Mao
forbes_bio: Charlwin Mao is the CEO of  Shanghai-headquartered social and e-commerce platform Xiaohongshu.
Mao co-founded the company with Miranda Qu in 2013.
Earlier in his career, he worked at Bain Consulting and Bain Capital.

name: Samir Mane
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Samir Mane is the founder and president of BALFIN Group, an investment conglomerate based in Tirana, Albania.
BALFIN owns shopping malls and electronics retail and toy stores in the western Balkans, plus a bank and luxury real estate developments in Albania.
Mane fled Albania's communist regime in 1991 and moved to Austria as a refugee; in 1993, he started selling domestic appliances to his native country.
He launched Neptun, a chain of electronics stores, in Albania in 1998 and moved back to Albania in 2005 to open the country's first shopping mall.
BALFIN also owns real estate in the U.S., Canada and Austria as well as logistics parks and a private university in Albania.
forbes_facts: Mane would sleep in trucks on the two-day journey from Vienna to Tirana when he sold appliances in the early 1990s.

name: Bharat Desai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2018-2022)
forbes_bio: Bharat Desai founded IT consulting and outsourcing company Syntel with his wife Neerja Sethi from their apartment in Troy, Michigan in 1980.
In 2018 French IT firm Atos SE acquired Syntel for $3.4 billion in cash.
Atos sued Desai, accusing him of hiding liabilities ahead of the merger; the case was dismissed in 2023.
In its first year, Syntel generated just $30,000 in sales; before it was acquired, annual revenue grew to more than $900 million.
Desai, who was Syntel's chairman, was born in Kenya, raised in India and came to the U.S. in 1976 as a programmer for Tata.
forbes_facts: Desai and Sethi started the company with just $2,000.
The couple met in the U.S. while working for pioneering IT firm, Tata Consultancy Services, the company they went on to emulate.

name: Henrique Dubugras
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2025)
forbes_bio: Henrique Dubugras is co-CEO of Brex, a fintech startup aiming to overhaul the corporate credit card.
He met his cofounder Pedro Franceschi through a Twitter argument in 2012, when they were both high school seniors living in their home country of Brazil.
In 2013, the cofounders launched a payments startup called Pagar.me for small business in Brazil and sold it to a larger Brazilian rival in 2015.
Dubugras grew up in Sao Paulo, Brazil, and attended Stanford with Franceschi for less than a year before they dropped out to start Brex in 2017.
He became a billionaire in January 2022, when Brex, based in California, raised money from private investors who valued Brex $12.3 billion.

name: Kim Sang-yeol
forbes_bio: Kim Sang-yeol is founder and chairman of Hoban Construction, one of South Korea's top builders.
Kim rose to billionaire status in 2019, after an internal merger more than doubled the net assets of his developer.
Kim expanded Hoban during the 1997-1998 Asian financial crisis by snapping up properties when prices were at an all-time low.
In an early plan for succession, his eldest son, Kim Dae-heon, was promoted to Hoban's vice president in 2019 and is now its largest shareholder.
Forbes Asia has attributed the fortune to the elder Kim, who likely maintains control.
forbes_facts: Kim was born to a poor farming family in the southern province of Jeolla.
At just 28 years old, he started Hoban with less than $95,000 in capital and a headcount of five staff members.

name: Samih Sawiris
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2015); Hurun Global (2014-2020)
forbes_bio: Samih Sawiris is the middle son of Egypt's wealthiest family, and founder and chairman of Orascom Development Holding, which builds and operates resorts in Egypt, Montenegro and Switzerland.
His brothers, Nassef and Naguib, are also billionaires and his son, Naguib Samih, is chairman of the board at Orascom Development.
He and his brothers all own stakes in publicly-traded Orascom Construction, the company established by their father in 1950.
Sawiris is also a founder and board member of the Sawiris Foundation for Social Development (SFSD), which seeks to create sustainable job opportunities for Egyptians.

name: Markus Persson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Markus "Notch" Persson made his fortune selling the rights to his game Minecraft to Microsoft.
In September 2014, after selling 15 million copies of Minecraft across gaming consoles, Persson sold out to Microsoft in a $2.5 billion cash deal.
Persson has since been jetting around the world while programming new games in his spare time.
An avid social media user, Persson has been open about the downsides of instant success as he used Reddit to express loneliness.
Persson has said he mostly spends money on computer gear and traveling, though he bought a $70 million home in Beverly Hill in December 2014.
forbes_facts: Persson created Minecraft as a hobby project, and released the boxy designed game in indie-game forums, which won immediate popularity.
Persson is a member of high IQ society Mensa.

name: Leo Huang
forbes_bio: Leo Huang is chairman and CEO of Chroma ATE, a supplier of automatic testing equipment for sectors such as automotive and semiconductors.
The company's power testing equipment is finding increasing uses worldwide amid exponential electricity usage due to the AI boom.
He cofounded Chroma in 1984 with alumni of Taiwan's National Chiao Tung University, including Warren Chen who is also a billionaire.
The company went public in Taiwan in 1996.
Leo's son, David, sits on Chroma's board.

name: Christoph Zeller
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Christopher Zeller controls Ivoclar Vivadent, a closely-held maker of dental products and systems based in Schaan, Principality of Liechtenstein.
ounded in 1923 focusing on the production of artificial teeth, the company was bought by Zeller's grandfather, Dr. Adolf Schneider, in 1948.
Zeller served as CEO from 1990 to 2003. He served on the company's supervisory board until 2025, after having stepped down as chairman in 2019.
Today, Ivoclar Vivadent has subsidiaries in more than 50 countries, employs around 3,600 people and generates annual revenue in excess of $900 million.
forbes_facts: Zeller's wife, Christina, also serves on the supervisory board.
